articles.title: India's First Bullet Train to Be Inaugurated in 2027: Vaishnaw - Hindusthan Samachar English
articles.content: New Delhi, 09 September (H.S.): Union Information and Broadcasting and Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Wednesday that the country’s first bullet train will be inaugurated in 2027. He said the indigenously manufactured bullet train is expected to begin track trials in May-June 2027, following which it will be inaugurated after the completion of testing. At a press conference convened to brief the media on the decisions taken by the Cabinet, Vaishnaw said the inauguration of the bullet train has been scheduled for 2027. Initially, there were plans to commence operations on an approximately 50-kilometre stretch between Surat and Bilimora, but the plan has now been expanded to cover the first section from Surat to Vapi, spanning around 100 kilometres, which is scheduled to be opened in 2027. The construction of this section is targeted for completion by December 2026. The minister said the construction of one coach of the bullet train being manufactured in India was completed last week. The coach will subsequently undergo pressure and climate-related tests, while other works, including interior fittings, will also be completed. The train is planned to be brought onto the tracks for testing by May-June next year. Following the completion of trials, the Prime Minister will inaugurate the service. It may be recalled that Vaishnaw had also said in Vadodara a day earlier that the country’s indigenously manufactured bullet train would be brought onto the tracks for testing in May-June 2027 and could be inaugurated two to four months after the trials. He had said that the first body frame of the train had been completed and sent for testing. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor has a total length of 508 kilometres. Work on the project is underway in Gujarat, Maharashtra and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli. The proposed bullet train will have a maximum operating speed of 320 kilometres per hour.
